chunks: As for the saying that the situation is confusing and it cannot be decided whether Imam Hasan (peace be upon him) sired a son or not, and until the birth of his son is established, we will adhere to the Imamate of Hasan; it is also invalidated through our assertion that no time can be without an Imam, because we know Hasan (peace be upon him) is dead just as we know many other people to be dead, and we will prove the birth of his son as well, so their claim is also falsified.

ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology refute the doubt about the birth of Imam Hasan al-Askari's son?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi addresses the 'Ambiguity Sect' (Al-Mu'tabirah) who doubted the birth of Imam Hasan al-Askari due to his prolonged concealment, arguing that their uncertainty is invalid because the principle of *Hujjah* (Proof) necessitates an Imam in every age. He asserts that just as the death of Imam Hasan is a known historical fact, the birth of his son is equally established to ensure the continuity of divine guidance, a point he further substantiates by detailing the specific circumstances of the birth.
